html:
The capture of Saigon, capital of South Vietnam, by North Vietnamese forces on 30 April 1975. It ended the Vietnam War.

American combat troops had left in 1973 after the Paris peace accords, and the United States Congress cut aid to the south. In March 1975 the North's army, under General Văn Tiến Dũng, began what it expected to be a two year campaign. Instead the southern army collapsed. The highlands, Huế and Đà Nẵng fell within weeks, and columns raced south, supplied down the Ho Chi Minh trail and new roads.

As the city was surrounded, the United States ran its largest helicopter evacuation, Operation Frequent Wind, lifting Americans and thousands of South Vietnamese from the embassy and other sites to ships offshore. On 30 April a tank broke through the gates of the presidential palace, and the last southern president surrendered.

Vietnam was formally reunified in 1976, and Saigon was renamed Ho Chi Minh City after Hồ Chí Minh. Re-education camps and hardship that followed drove the exodus of the boat people.
sum: The capture of Saigon, capital of South Vietnam, by North Vietnamese forces on 30 April 1975. It ended the Vietnam War.
